sentences.text: 2. The 1st respondent/claimant filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act R/w Rule 455 of the Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Rules, seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- along with costs and interest for the injuries sustained by him in the accident that took place on 30.12.2015.

It is stated that, the said accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the 2nd respondent/driver of APSRTC bus bearing registration No.AP 29 Z 0379.
3.

Upon contest, the said petition was partly allowed by order dated 05.10.2018, awarding compensation of Rs.2,27,050/- together with subsequent interest @7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by respondents No.1 to 4 therein.

4. Questioning the said order, the present appeal has been filed on the ground that the claimant/1st respondent herein failed to establish that the 2nd respondent (driver of APSRTC Bus) drove the TCDS,J vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
It is further stated that the Tribunal erroneously considered the income of the 1st respondent as Rs.61,000/- per annum, despite no documentary evidence is filed in support of his claim.
5. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.
No representation for the respondents.
Perused the material available on record.

6. The learned counsel for the appellants would strenuously contend that, the 1st respondent miserably failed to establish that the 2nd respondent (driver of APSRTC Bus) drove the vehicle in Apstrc vs K. Srinu on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172187555/
2 rash and negligent manner.

The said submission of the learned counsel for the appellants cannot be countenanced, inasmuch as, on perusal of the record, it is succinctly clear that the 2nd respondent/driver himself admitted during the course of cross- examination that, a crime was registered in Crime No.223 of 2015 on the file of III Town Police Station, Visakhapatnam, against him.
His cross-examination would further reveal that he also paid a fine of Rs.15,000/-, admitting that he drove the bus in rash and negligent manner.
The 1st respondent/claimant has filed Exs.A1 to A10 documents to show that the 1st respondent has paid the said fine amount.

In view of the categorical admission made by the 2nd respondent herein, coupled with the exhibits filed by the 1st TCDS,J respondent, it is proved the 2nd respondent drove the bus in rash and negligent thereby the 1st respondent sustained injuries.
7. The other ground raised in the appeal is that the 1st respondent/claimant did not file any documentary proof to show that he is earning an amount of Rs.61,000/- per annum.
The submission made by the learned counsel for the appellants cannot be accepted, for the reason that the 1st respondent/claimant filed Ex.A7, a copy of Income tax return, in support of his claim.

By taking into consideration of the income tax returns filed by the 1st respondent for the year 2015-2016, the tribunal has come to the conclusion that the income of the claimant as Rs.61,000/-
per annum.
Income tax return is marked as Ex.A7 before the tribunal.
Therefore, the contention of the appellants cannot be accepted.

Further, the Doctor who conducted surgery for the injuries sustained by the claimant has categorically deposed that he implanted ORIF with fibula plating and screws under spinal anesthesia, and the wound was closed above knee slab.
Further, the 1st respondent/claimant was operating to the fracture of his left hand distal radius and plating was done and POP bandage was applied.
In view of the injuries sustained, the 1st respondent is having stiffness of left wrist and left ankle.
In view of the same, it is clear that the claimant suffered disability of 7%.

Therefore, while awarding compensation to the 1st TCDS,J respondent/claimant,
the Tribunal had taken into consideration the relevant facts and awarded an amount of Rs.2,27,050/- towards compensation.
Though several grounds are raised in the present appeal, the appellants could not substantiate the same by placing relevant evidence.
8. In view of the above, this Court does not find any illegality in the order impugned and accordingly the present appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE T.C.D.SEKHAR Date: 07.08.2025 KGR Apstrc vs K. Srinu on 7 August, 2025
